info.title: Oneirodex API
info.description: Self-hosted multi-user game library API. Authenticate with session cookies or Authorization: Bearer gt_<prefix>_<secret>.

StoreSyncJob.description: One live ownership sync attempt. outcome carries only catalogue text; a running job whose heartbeat is older than ten minutes is reported as failed/interrupted.

200.description: Envelope with up to 50 titles and next_after_id cursor. Each title has id, match_revision, match_reviewed and an ACL-filtered matched_game_uuid.

get.summary: List implemented store capabilities separately from account readiness
get.description: Read-only registry; no provider requests or credentials. Unsupported operations remain unavailable. policy_enabled is operator policy, not successful account authentication.

401.description: Authentication required; session authentication may redirect to login

get.summary: The current member's connection status per provider
get.description: One contract for first-run, Settings and admin repair. Derived from stored facts only (operator policy, linked account, credential source, recorded titles, latest sync job); no provider request, no credential. connected means linked and the last sync did not fail, not that a provider would accept the sign-in now.

200.description: Envelope with sync_enabled and one entry per registered provider

cancellable.description: The adapter checks for cancellation between provider pages (GOG, Epic, Amazon). Single-request adapters are never cancellable.

source.description: Which sign-in a sync would use. `unknown`: saved before LIB-04 on a server that has a household sign-in for this store, so it may be a household copy; reconnecting settles it.

401.description: Authentication required; session authentication may redirect to login

post.summary: Run one live ownership sync as a recorded job
post.description: Existing per-store routes (steam, gog, epic, amazon, xbox, psn). Failures return a fixed catalogue sentence and detail {reason, message, action, retryable, audience}; exception text, request URLs and upstream bodies are never returned. A cancelled sync returns 200 with cancelled=true and nothing saved.

200.description: synced, matched, store, job (StoreSyncJob) and summary; job.status succeeded, partial or cancelled. A succeeded job may carry job.outcome as a warning (library_not_visible: the provider returned no visible library).

400.description: not_connected, credential_missing, device_serial_missing, credential_rejected (member sign-in expired or revoked), household_credential_rejected (the operator's household sign-in was refused; admin-fixable), server_key_missing, client_package_missing

403.description: sync_disabled or opt_in_required (detail carries the reason)

409.description: sync_in_progress (another sync for this member and store is running) or store_busy (a connect/disconnect for it is in progress)

502.description: Upstream: access_denied, rate_limited, upstream_unavailable, network_error, blocked_by_policy, invalid_response

post.summary: Link or reconnect a store account (existing per-store routes)
post.description: Bodies are validated (unknown fields and over-long values return 422). Tokens are stored server-side and never returned. Refused with 409 while a sync or another link change for the same store is running, so a finishing sync cannot overwrite a new sign-in. Only a new sign-in (or, for Steam, a different Steam ID) counts as a reconnect that clears an earlier sign-in failure.

delete.summary: Disconnect: remove the link, its recorded titles, their match decisions and its sync history

post.summary: Ask a running sync to stop at its next provider page
post.description: Honoured only by adapters that read several pages (GOG, Epic, Amazon). Steam, Xbox and PlayStation make one provider call and are refused with not_cancellable rather than shown a fake cancellation.

202.description: cancel_requested recorded. The sync stops at its next provider page and reports cancelled with nothing saved; a sync already writing its results finishes and reports succeeded.

404.description: No live sync exists for this store

get.description: States, reason codes, record counts, credential source and household configuration as presence flags. Never credentials, external account IDs or title lists. Non-admin sessions are redirected to login.

post.summary: Member-facing freshness sweep of the library
post.description: Re-probes titles the caller can see, oldest-checked first, in one bounded batch — each title is a live store request, so an unbounded sweep would hold a request thread for minutes and rate-limit the caller. The inbox only reads what a probe already found; this is what makes a probe happen. Returns remaining so the UI can say how much of the library is still unswept.

only_stale.description: Skip titles probed in the last 24h.

200.description: ok envelope with requested, checked, behind[], behind_count, errors[], remaining, limit, only_stale

500.description: ok:false, error_code internal — results could not be saved

post.summary: Start or queue a scan for one library
post.description: Admin only. Body/query: library_uuid (required), folder (defaults to the library's last_scan_folder), scan_mode folders|files, remove_missing, download_missing_images, force_updates_extras, queue_policy queue|force / force_parallel. Response uses the scan-queue contract, not the api_ok envelope: { status: 'queued'|'started'|'rejected', job_id, position, message, risk? }.

400.description: rejected — no library_uuid, or no folder and no last_scan_folder

409.description: rejected — a scan is already running and queue_policy did not allow it

get.description: Stable 200 with empty releases when IGDB off/empty. Query: days_ahead, days_behind, limit.

get.summary: Systems this title exists on, with per-core launchers
get.description: Every copy of the same title across the caller's accessible libraries, one entry per library row, each carrying its own play options and a launch URL per browser-playable emulator core. Titles are paired by normalised name because Game.igdb_id and Game.slug are both unique, so cross-platform copies cannot share either. Always returns at least the requested game, so a caller never has to special-case a single-system title.

post.description: The email address is optional. Without one — or without SMTP — the invite is still created and its URL is returned for the inviter to pass on directly. `emailed` reports whether anything was actually sent.
